payload.system: Return only the requested structured result. Classify consensus distance without deciding the full chapter's persuasiveness.

messages.content:
You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Knowing, to know

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES
RESPONSE A
{
  "primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching and biblical scholarship, 'to know' (Hebrew yada'; Greek ginōskō) is overwhelmingly interpreted as denoting intimate, experiential, relational knowledge rather than mere intellectual or factual awareness. 'Knowing God' is read as personal communion and covenant relationship with Him, and being 'known' by God as His personal, saving recognition and acceptance. Eternal life itself is defined as this relational knowledge (John 17:3).",
  "primary_basis": [
    "John 17:3 ('this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God')",
    "Jeremiah 9:23-24 ('let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me')",
    "Jeremiah 31:34 ('they shall all know me, from the least to the greatest')",
    "Hosea 6:6 ('I desire... the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings')",
    "Hosea 4:1, 4:6 (Israel destroyed for lack of knowledge of God)",
    "Matthew 7:23 ('I never knew you; depart from me')",
    "Philippians 3:8-10 ('that I may know him and the power of his resurrection')",
    "1 John 2:3-4; 4:7-8 (knowing God evidenced by obedience and love)",
    "Galatians 4:9 ('now that you know God, or rather are known by God')",
    "Psalm 1:6 ('the LORD knows the way of the righteous')",
    "Exodus 33:12-17 ('I know you by name')",
    "John 10:14-15 ('I know my own and my own know me')"
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "Sexual/marital euphemism: 'to know' as the idiom for sexual intercourse, widely treated as an extension of the intimacy sense and often used homiletically to illustrate that biblical knowledge is union, not information.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 4:1 ('Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived')",
        "Genesis 4:17; 4:25",
        "Genesis 19:8; Judges 11:39; 19:22-25",
        "Matthew 1:25 ('knew her not until she had given birth')",
        "Luke 1:34 ('since I know not a man')"
      ],
      "prominence": "dominant"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Covenantal election: 'to know' as God's sovereign choice or election of persons/Israel ('foreknew' = 'fore-loved/chose'), a standard reading in Reformed and much critical scholarship, drawing on ancient Near Eastern treaty language where 'know' means 'recognize as covenant partner.'",
      "basis": [
        "Amos 3:2 ('You only have I known of all the families of the earth')",
        "Romans 8:29 ('those whom he foreknew he also predestined')",
        "Genesis 18:19 ('I have known/chosen him')",
        "Jeremiah 1:5 ('before I formed you in the womb I knew you')",
        "2 Timothy 2:19 ('the Lord knows those who are his')"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Moral-experiential autonomy: in the phrase 'knowledge of good and evil' (Genesis 2-3), 'knowing' read as seizing autonomous moral determination or experiential acquaintance with evil, rather than gaining information; variously nuanced as moral autonomy, maturity, or comprehensive knowledge (a merism).",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 2:9, 2:17",
        "Genesis 3:5, 3:22 ('you will be like God, knowing good and evil')",
        "Deuteronomy 1:39 (children who 'have no knowledge of good or evil')"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Salvific gnosis: knowledge as secret, esoteric insight that itself saves, characteristic of ancient Gnosticism and rejected by mainstream Christianity; New Testament warnings against 'knowledge falsely so called' are read as opposing this view.",
      "basis": [
        "1 Timothy 6:20 ('contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge')",
        "1 Corinthians 8:1 ('knowledge puffs up, but love builds up')",
        "Colossians 2:8, 2:18 (often read against proto-gnostic tendencies)"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Purely intellectual/propositional knowledge: 'to know' as cognitive assent to facts or doctrine; generally treated in Christian interpretation as insufficient by itself, with James cited to show even demons possess such knowledge.",
      "basis": [
        "James 2:19 ('even the demons believe—and shudder')",
        "Romans 1:21 ('although they knew God, they did not honor him')",
        "Titus 1:16 ('they profess to know God, but deny him by their works')"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "There is a broad, recognizable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and academic biblical scholarship that biblical 'knowing' is relational and experiential (Hebrew yada'), embracing intimacy, covenant loyalty, and obedience, in contrast to Greek notions of detached intellectual cognition (a contrast sometimes overstated in older word-study literature, as critics like James Barr noted). The sexual euphemism (Gen 4:1) and the covenantal-election sense (Amos 3:2; Rom 8:29) are standard, widely acknowledged sub-senses of the same relational root rather than competing symbols. Assessment made blind to the author's material, as instructed."
}

RESPONSE B
{
  "primary_meaning": "When “know” carries theological or symbolic force, it most commonly denotes personal, experiential, and covenantal relationship—especially intimate communion with God—rather than mere possession of information. Such knowledge is often understood as involving recognition, love, trust, and obedience.",
  "primary_basis": [
    "Jeremiah 9:23–24 — true boasting is in understanding and knowing the Lord.",
    "Hosea 6:6 — God desires steadfast love and the knowledge of God rather than sacrifice.",
    "John 10:14–15 — Jesus and his sheep mutually “know” one another, modeled on the Father-Son relationship.",
    "John 17:3 — eternal life is defined as knowing the Father and Jesus Christ.",
    "Philippians 3:8–10 — Paul seeks to know Christ through participation in his life, suffering, and resurrection.",
    "1 John 2:3–4 — knowing God is evidenced by keeping his commandments.",
    "1 Corinthians 8:1–3 — merely possessing knowledge is contrasted with loving God and being known by him."
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "Ordinary intellectual or propositional awareness: knowing facts, truths, distinctions, or doctrine without necessarily implying personal relationship.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 3:22",
        "Luke 11:52",
        "Romans 2:20",
        "1 Corinthians 8:1–2",
        "James 4:17"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Sexual intimacy: “to know” functions as a Hebrew-influenced euphemism for sexual intercourse.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 4:1",
        "Genesis 4:17",
        "Genesis 19:5–8",
        "Judges 19:22–25",
        "Matthew 1:25",
        "Luke 1:34"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Covenantal acknowledgment, choice, or belonging: God’s “knowing” someone may signify recognizing that person or people as his own, sometimes with connotations of election.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 18:19",
        "Amos 3:2",
        "Matthew 7:23",
        "Galatians 4:9",
        "2 Timothy 2:19"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Discernment or recognition—identifying a person, condition, meaning, or spiritual reality.",
      "basis": [
        "Matthew 7:16–20",
        "Luke 24:30–31",
        "John 7:17",
        "1 Corinthians 2:11–14"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Special esoteric or secret revelation available only to a spiritual elite, as in some Gnostic or esoteric systems.",
      "basis": [
        "1 Corinthians 8:1–3 and Colossians 2:2–4 are sometimes discussed in relation to claims of privileged knowledge, though the texts themselves caution against deceptive or prideful forms of knowledge."
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": false,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "“Know” is not a fixed biblical symbol with one meaning across all contexts; it is a broad verb whose sense depends heavily on its object and literary setting. There is strong consensus that “knowing God” usually has relational and experiential force, but no settled symbolic interpretation governs every occurrence of “know.”"
}

RESPONSE C
{
  "primary_meaning": "Intimate, experiential, personal relationship or union (especially with God), as distinct from mere intellectual or propositional awareness",
  "primary_basis": [
    "John 17:3 (eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ)",
    "Genesis 4:1 (Adam knew Eve and she conceived—intimate/relational sense)",
    "Hosea 4:1, 6; 6:3, 6 (knowledge of God as relational/covenantal fidelity)",
    "Jeremiah 9:23-24; 31:34 (knowing the Lord as true boast and new-covenant reality)",
    "Matthew 7:23; 25:12 (I never knew you—personal recognition/relationship)",
    "Philippians 3:8-10 (knowing Christ experientially, power of resurrection, sharing sufferings)",
    "1 Corinthians 8:3; Galatians 4:9 (being known by God)",
    "1 John 2:3-4; 4:7-8 (knowing God evidenced in keeping commandments and love)"
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "Sexual intercourse or carnal knowledge (euphemistic use of the verb)",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 4:1, 17, 25; 19:5, 8; 24:16; 38:26",
        "Judges 11:39; 19:22, 25",
        "1 Samuel 1:19; 1 Kings 1:4",
        "Matthew 1:25 (did not know her until...)"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Intellectual, cognitive, or factual awareness/information",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 3:5, 22 (knowledge of good and evil)",
        "Proverbs and wisdom literature on knowledge/skill",
        "Many NT uses of ginōskō/oida for ordinary cognition or recognition"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Covenantal loyalty, obedience, or recognition of God's character and ways",
      "basis": [
        "Hosea and prophetic literature (knowledge of God vs. cultic ritual)",
        "Jeremiah 22:15-16 (doing justice and righteousness = knowing the Lord)",
        "Psalm 9:10; 36:10; 91:14"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Mystical or contemplative union/participation in divine life",
      "basis": [
        "John 14–17 and 1 John (abiding, mutual indwelling language)",
        "Later patristic, medieval, and mystical writers reading these texts"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "Biblical Hebrew yadaʿ and Greek ginōskō/oida carry a broad semantic range; Christian teaching and biblical scholarship commonly distinguish the frequent relational/experiential/intimate sense (especially 'knowing God') from purely intellectual knowledge, while also recognizing the sexual euphemism and ordinary cognitive uses in context. No single monovalent 'symbol' is claimed for every occurrence, but the intimate/relational reading is the dominant interpretive emphasis when the term is treated symbolically or theologically."
}

BOOK ENTRY
Covenant relationship proven by obedience — the intimate “knew” of marriage; a stranger is one not known.

BOOK'S COMMON-VIEW NOTE, IF PRESENT
(none)

SCRIPTURE REFERENCES PRINTED WITH THE ENTRY
(Gen 4:1; Hos 4:6; Matt 7:23; 1 John 2:3-4) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Genesis 4:1 — And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.
Hosea 4:6 — My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
Matthew 7:23 — And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
1 John 2:3 — And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.
1 John 2:4 — He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

- MATCH: substantially the same meaning as the recognizable consensus.
- REFINED: compatible with the consensus but materially sharper, narrower,
  broader, or more precisely supported.
- DIVERGENT: contradicts or displaces a recognizable common interpretation.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus covers the book's central claim; the book
  stakes a meaning not represented by the blind responses.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
